excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: The state root is included in the block so the state can't contain the block root itself, however you can calculate it by taking the latest_valid_header from the state, setting the state_root field to the hash_tree_root of the state then getting the hash_tree_root of that header.

excerpts.author: wowsuchname.eth
excerpts.content: What would happen with the Ethereum network in case of a solar superstorm that would disrupt all intercontinental internet cables and take down all satellite communications?

excerpts.author: wowsuchname.eth
excerpts.content: Here is a thorough paper estimating the changes of this happening at up to 12% in the next decade: https://www.ics.uci.edu/~sabdujyo/papers/sigcomm21-cme.pdf

excerpts.author: wowsuchname.eth
excerpts.content: I imagine it would fork into a few parts, each behaving as if all the other validators are offline.

excerpts.author: wowsuchname.eth
excerpts.content: Any change of a reconciliation after such an event?

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
Yes, especially if the sides of the partition can come back together before enough time has passed to achieve finality. On a split network it takes several weeks to leak out the balances of the partitioned validators to the point where the remainder can achieve finality.

Even if finality were achieved, people could switch chains based on social consensus and one side may prevail as the “true Eth”

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: (in case of no-finality the partition heals automatically)

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: From theory to reality though there's a gap, I think every experiment Yorick did with very long splits ended up with Prysm and Teku on a different fork

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: hey folks, just wonder what it the current proposal for daily withdrawal limits post Shanghai and if the request to withdraw exceeds that limit, what's the rule to decide who gets the chance on that day? Thanks!

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content:
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/capella/beacon-chain.md
Basically just a loop over the validators, starting at 0. No queue (there is an exit queue of course, but that remains unchanged)

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: thanks, is there a max withdrawal limit per withdrawal for each validator or e.g. if I have one validator and want to withdrawal 64 eth, does that take 2 weeks?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: No. Take a look at `get_expected_withdrawals` and `process_withdrawals`.

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: Thanks, a few questions, seems is_fully_withdrawable_validator only checks if balance > 0? does that mean this is always true if validator gets the credential?

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: And does it check these conditions for every epoch?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: there's three requirements as you can see, one of which is `> 0.` They all have to be satisfied.

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: yeah, I am just thinking if is_fully_withdrawable_validator always happen before is_partially_withdrawable_validator

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: the condition is validator.withdrawable_epoch <= epoch, I guess

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: That's what the code says yes.

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: thanks, how withdrawable_epoch is decided?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#initiate_validator_exit

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: So like minimum 27 hours after signing/broadcasting an exit message, assuming no exit queue. If the exit queue is filled up, it might be a while longer of course.

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: thanks, will FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH be the first epoch post Shanghai fork?

excerpts.author: rays5439
excerpts.content: sorry how the exit queue works? is it constrained by some max withdrawal limit per epoch, etc.

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Yep, similar to entry/deposit queue. A maximum number per epoch, I think like 6 now.
